note: Anchor ~1960 (~$5.9k 2011$PPP). High-growth miracle: heavy industry + export manufacturing, ~35% savings/investment engine; public debt tiny. Doubled GDP/cap by ~1968 (~8yr).
Oil shocks halve growth but still rapid; 1974 inflation ~23%; fiscal stimulus starts lifting debt. Already high-income - escaped trap ~1970.
Mature high-income; chronic trade surpluses; Plaza Accord 1985; asset bubble inflates late-decade.
Bubble bursts - 'Lost Decade'. Growth collapses; public debt EXPLODES (65->100%+) AFTER catch-up complete. Debt was a consequence of stagnation, not the growth model.
Anchor ~1980 (~$6.5k). Heavy-Chemical-Industry drive matures into chaebol export manufacturing; 1980 recession then boom; inflation tamed from ~28% (1980). Very low public debt.
Boom continues; savings ~37% > investment by late-decade; 1997 Asian crisis + IMF bailout a sharp but temporary shock. Debt still ~12%.
High-income (OECD 1996); electronics/autos/shipbuilding move up value chain. Clearly escaped middle-income trap. Doubled GDP/cap ~1980->1990 (~10yr).
Advanced economy; growth normalises; aging demographics. Public debt still moderate (~40%) - low-debt catch-up throughout.

Anchor ~2005 (~$6.6k). WTO-era boom: export manufacturing ('world's factory') + record ~45-50% investment/savings. Govt debt modest but total economy debt rising fast. Doubled GDP/cap ~2005->2013 (~8yr).

Growth slows; rebalancing toward domestic demand; property + LGFV/SOE debt buildup (broad total ~280% GDP). Reached upper-middle/high-income threshold (~$13k) ~2023-24. Trap-escape genuine but debt overhang is the open risk. Track incomplete (~20yr elapsed).
Anchor ~1890 (~$5.7k). Gilded Age industrialization on a huge INTERNAL market (not export-led); gold-standard deflation; very low federal debt. Immigration-fed labor + capital deepening.
Becomes world's largest economy; mass production, electrification. Low trade share - growth driven by continental scale + institutions/innovation.
WWI boom then 1920-21 slump; debt rises to ~33% (1919) financing war; high wartime inflation.

Roaring Twenties; federal debt paid down ~33%->16% by 1930; autos/consumer durables. Doubled GDP/cap ~1890->~1929 (~40yr, per-capita ~2%/yr; rest of GDP growth was population). Escaped decisively - the frontier.
Anchor ~1870 (~$5.0k). 'Workshop of the world' - free trade, HIGH export share but LOW domestic investment (capital exported to empire/US). Not catch-up but the leader being caught.
'Long Depression' deflation; relative decline begins; Victorian debt paydown continues.
Overtaken by US and Germany in per-capita income; the 'British climacteric' - slowing productivity.
Edwardian maturity; slow growth; debt at ~200-year low (~30% by 1913). Doubled GDP/cap ~1870->~1935 (~60-65yr) - SLOWEST case: mature frontier, low investment, capital export.
Anchor ~1890 (~$5.3k). Second Industrial Revolution: steel, chemicals, electricals; technical education + universal (Hausbank) finance; cartels. Strong fundamentals.
Overtakes Britain in key industries; catches the income frontier (~$8.7k by 1913). High investment ~23%.
WWI CATASTROPHE: debt-financed total war, defeat, Versailles reparations. Catch-up derailed. (1918-23 inflation -> hyperinflation, no clean CPI.)

1923 HYPERINFLATION wipes nominal debt; brief Weimar recovery 1924-28 then 1929 Depression. Only reached its 1913 income again ~1930s, collapsed in WWII (1950=$3.9k). Cautionary: strong catch-up fundamentals RESET ~60yr by war/institutional collapse. High-income secured only via post-1950 Wirtschaftswunder.

CONTRAST/STALLED case. Anchor ~1975 (~$5.9k). 'Brazilian miracle' ending: import-substitution industrialization funded by external borrowing; already high inflation; LOW savings ~20% vs Asia's 35-45%.
'LOST DECADE': 1982 external debt crisis, hyperinflation. Middle-income trap sets in - growth stops, exports don't upgrade.
Real Plan (1994) finally stabilizes inflation but growth stays weak; manufacturing export base thin.

Commodity boom then stagnation. STILL STUCK in upper-middle income. ~$5.9k (1975) -> only ~$14k by 2019: ~40+yr to barely 2x vs Asia's ~8-10yr. Trap = low savings/investment, high inflation/debt, no sustained export-manufacturing upgrade.
